text:
Sam: quick heads-up — saw a reproducible stall in staging where prefetch workers and eviction sweeps deadlock. stack trace attached, affecting a handful of requests.
Alisha: can you drop the trace/link?
Sam: pasted gist: ```prefetch_worker.acquire(shard_lock)
evict_sweep.acquire(tenant_lock)
evict_sweep.wait_for(prefetch_release)
prefetch_worker.wait_for(evict_quiesce) // cycle```
Ben: ugh. looks like inverted lock ordering between the two subsystems. did we ever document locking discipline for shard vs tenant?
Maria: i saw a similar pattern in the chaos runs when demotion frequency was 10s and prefetch concurrency > 3. cold-requests pile up then everything stalls.
Chen: short idea: change prefetch to acquire tenant lock first, then shard. that makes ordering consistent but we need to audit hot paths for perf regressions.
Sam: ordering flip is simplest correctness-wise but could hurt throughput for high-rt workloads. grabbing tenant lock earlier expands critical section.
Alisha: alternative: keep ordering but make eviction do a best-effort preempt (steal soft-lease) instead of waiting. eviction would RPC to prefetch worker: `STEAL_PREFIX(token)` and prefetch either yields or hands metadata.
Ben: that steal RPC is attractive — avoids global lock reorders. downside: increases RPC surface and requires idempotent handoff logic. correctness proof gets messier.
Kai: i can run a bench for lock-order flip vs steal RPC. will test throughput and tail latency with our standard hotset (10k keys, skew .9).
Maria: add to bench variants: prefetch concurrency 1..8, demote interval 2s/10s/30s. measure 95/99th lat + stall rate.
Chen: another middle ground: acquire tenant lock in shared/read mode for prefetch and exclusive/write mode for eviction. reduces contention while preserving ordering. but we must ensure lock implementation supports upgrade safely.
Sam: good point — we currently don't have a clean upgrade path; upgrade can deadlock itself unless we use try_lock+retry.
Alisha: metrics suggestion: add "lock_wait_chain" sampling (small stack of which locks are held when waiting). we can detect cycles in prod before they hit wide.
Ben: agree. add histograms: `lock_wait_time{lock_type, holder_role}` and a sampled "waiter_chain" tag. low overhead sampling.
Sam: quick patch idea (short-term mitigation): introduce bounded wait with backoff in eviction. instead of blocking forever, eviction backs off and re-enqueues token for later. that buys us stability while we design long-term fix.
Maria: that will reduce coldness risk but may increase dirty memory pressure. need to pair with a tighter eviction budget so we don't OOM.
evict-bot: created INF-2345: "stalls: cooperative-prefetch-eviction-deadlock" and INF-2346: "telemetry: lock_wait_chain sampling"
Kai: i'll run the microbench this afternoon and post results by EOD.
Ben: i'll sketch the steal-token proto + failure modes.
Chen: i'll prototype read-mode tenant lock and an upgrade-friendly try_lock loop.
Alisha: i'll add the telemetry PR and a staging canary gating rule (fail if stall_rate > 0.1%).
Sam: action list summarized: 1) Kai perf runs, 2) Ben proto for steal RPC, 3) Chen try-lock prototype, 4) Alisha telemetry/canary, 5) short-term bounded-wait patch. we'll reconvene tomorrow.
Maria: +1. thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
Sam: filing a follow-up postmortem note after we have bench data.
Alisha: FYI — when you add code snippets, follow the prefix cache lint for non-blocking handoff: `// handoff must be idempotent`
Ben: noted.
Chen: quick sketch of steal RPC (pseudo): ```rpc StealPrefix(tenant, prefix_id) returns {status, holder_info}; // on success eviction takes ownership, prefetch marks migrated or requeues```
Sam: cool. try to keep the proto tolerant of partial failures (retries, eager fallback to demote).
Kai: starting runs now. will ping in thread with perf matrix.
